turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?
turns.patient_response: Well, my work physical is what got me here, to be honest. The doctor doing the exam said my weight is too low. I mean, I don't really see it that way. To me, I just feel lighter on my feet when I play basketball, and... well, I'm not as weighed down when I'm working under cars at the garage. But they wanted me to come see someone about it, so here I am.

symptom_reasoning.S044: The patient reports being referred after a medical doctor at their work physical determined that their weight is too low.

turns.doctor_question: Are you doing anything on purpose to keep your weight low, like restricting how much you eat or exercising a lot?
turns.patient_response:
Well, I wouldn't say I'm doing it just to keep my weight low, but... I do keep things pretty strict, I guess. Most days I just stick to coffee in the morning. Then later on, I'll maybe have a small sandwich or just eat half of whatever is around the shop. 

Between work always running late and things being busy at the house, I just... I feel better sticking to my own simple rules with food. It keeps things straightforward for me.

symptom_reasoning.S043: The patient describes maintaining strict food rules and eating very small amounts, such as having only coffee in the morning and half a sandwich or half-portions later.

turns.doctor_question: When you think about the possibility of gaining weight, how does that make you feel? Are you afraid of it?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I guess I am. If I see the scale bump up even a pound, or if my work jeans feel tighter, I start thinking I'm getting soft. I just... I worry that if I put on weight, I'll be slower moving around cars at the garage, or slower up and down the court when I play. So, yeah, it definitely bothers me to think about gaining anything back.

symptom_reasoning.S045: The patient explicitly confirms feeling afraid and worried about gaining weight or putting on even a pound.

turns.doctor_question: When you look at yourself in the mirror or think about your body, do you see yourself as overweight, or do you recognize that you're actually on the thinner side?
turns.patient_response: Well, when I look in the mirror, I don't see myself as overweight, exactly, but I don't think I'm as skinny as the work doctor made it sound. I know people are worried about it, but I figure they're just making too much of it. I mean, I still show up for work every day, I take care of everything that needs doing around the house, and I still play ball on the weekends. If I was really that underweight, I wouldn't be able to do all that, right?

symptom_reasoning.S084: The patient minimizes the doctor's and others' concerns about their low weight, arguing that their functional capacity proves their low weight is not a serious issue.

turns.doctor_question: If I told you that your BMI is actually in the underweight range and you've lost a significant amount of weight, would you agree with that assessment, or do you still feel like you look about right or even heavier than that?
turns.patient_response: I guess I'd have to say I disagree. I mean, I know you doctors have your charts and numbers, but when I look at myself, I just see a guy who's staying lean so he can keep up. I don't feel like I look underweight. I just look... in shape, you know? Like I said, I'm still doing my job and playing basketball. I feel like I'm right where I need to be to get by.

symptom_reasoning.S084: The patient dismisses the doctor's assessment that his BMI is in the underweight range, denying that he looks underweight and minimizing concerns by stating he is just 'in shape' and functioning normally.

turns.doctor_question: Over the past year or so, how much weight would you say you've lost, or do you know approximately what you weighed before compared to now?
turns.patient_response: I'm not exactly sure on the exact number. I don't really keep track of it like that. I know I've dropped some weight over the last year, mostly just from working hard and keeping active, but I couldn't tell you what I weighed before versus now. I just know my clothes fit a bit looser.

turns.doctor_question: When you imagine yourself at a heavier weight—say 20 or 30 pounds more than you are now—how would that look to you? Would you see yourself as overweight or heavy in that scenario?
turns.patient_response:
Twenty or thirty pounds? Yeah, I'd definitely see myself as heavy if I put on that much. Honestly, if I see the scale bump up even just a single pound, or if my jeans start feeling a little tighter, I start thinking I'm getting soft. 

I don't want that. I just know if I gained weight, I'd be a lot slower moving around the shop and getting under cars, and definitely slower up and down the court on the weekends. So yeah, putting on that kind of weight is something I really want to avoid.

symptom_reasoning.S045: The patient expresses a strong desire to avoid gaining weight and reports anxiety over even a single pound increase or tighter clothing.

turns.doctor_question: If I showed you a photograph of someone who weighs the same as you do right now, with the same body shape and size, would you say that person looks underweight, normal weight, or overweight?
turns.patient_response: I don't know... it's hard to say without actually seeing the picture. I guess if they looked exactly like me, I'd probably just think they looked like a normal guy who stays active. I wouldn't call them underweight, no. I'd probably just think they look in shape, like they take care of themselves. I don't really look at myself and see someone who's too skinny, so I doubt I'd see it in someone else either.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever made yourself vomit, used laxatives, or done anything else to get rid of food after eating it?
turns.patient_response: No, I don't do anything like that. I've never made myself throw up or taken laxatives or anything. If I eat, I just... I just let it be. Like I said, I just burn it off working at the shop or staying active. I definitely don't mess around with making myself sick.

symptom_reasoning.S048: The patient explicitly denies ever making themselves vomit or using laxatives to expel food.

turns.doctor_question: When you look at yourself naked in the mirror right now, do you see areas of your body that you think look fat or flabby, or do you think your body looks appropriately lean for someone who's active?
turns.patient_response: I don't really see anything fat or flabby, no. I mean... when I look in the mirror, I just see a guy who stays active. I think I look appropriately lean, yeah. Just like a regular guy who works hard and keeps himself in decent shape. I don't really stand there picking apart my body or seeing flab everywhere. It just looks fine to me as is.

symptom_reasoning.S046: The patient explicitly denies distorted body image, stating they do not see anything fat or flabby and view themselves as appropriately lean.

turns.doctor_question: You mentioned you burn off food by working at the shop and staying active. Do you ever intentionally exercise more intensely or for longer periods specifically to make up for eating, or to prevent yourself from gaining weight?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. I mean, I work hard at the shop, but that's just my job. I'm on my feet all day, lifting things, moving around... it's just what I do. I don't go out of my way to run on a treadmill for hours or anything just because I ate a sandwich. The work keeps me active enough. I don't exercise just to burn off meals or stop myself from gaining weight.

symptom_reasoning.S047: The patient explicitly denies engaging in excessive exercise or driven workouts to compensate for food intake or prevent weight gain.
